writers.shapeNotes: Pure generator: calls z.toJSONSchema(zodSchema) (default io='output' mode) then `delete json.$schema`. Returns the JSON Schema object. Default mode is deliberate: with io='input', reviewResultSchema.qualityGate (which carries a Zod .default()) gets DROPPED from `required`, which would be looser than the hand-written contract; output mode keeps it required. z.toJSONSchema already emits additionalProperties:false on every z.object and correct per-object `required` sets, so no extra options are needed for strictness.

Returns `${JSON.stringify(zodToDriverJsonSchema(schema), null, 2)}\n` — identical byte format (2-space indent + trailing newline) to the prior hand-written fs.writeFileSync calls. Deterministic/byte-stable across calls (verified).

fs.mkdirSync(dirname, {recursive:true}) + fs.writeFileSync(schemaPath, serializeDriverJsonSchema(schema), 'utf8'). Exact replacement for the mkdir+writeFileSync logic that was inline in each of the 3 old writers.

baseline.consumers: The schema FILE written by these 3 writers is the driver-facing contract, consumed at runtime in src/worker-driver.ts buildInvocation: codex passes it via `--output-schema <spec.schemaPath>` (worker-driver.ts:79,97); claude reads the file, JSON.parse/stringify-roundtrips it, and inlines it via `--json-schema <json>` (worker-driver.ts:174-183). Both CLIs accept the generated shape — it is byte-equivalent (modulo the omitted $schema draft pointer, which the proven hand-written schemas also omitted) and key-ordering to the prior output. The RESULT artifact is then validated post-hoc with Zod safeParse against the SAME canonical schema: codex via validateResultArtifact (worker-driver.ts:116-139, schema = spec.resultSchema ?? workerResultSchema), claude in finalize (worker-driver.ts:219-251). cli.ts selects which writer to call per role and passes reviewResultSchema/overseerDecisionSchema as spec.resultSchema for the review/overseer runs, keeping held-to == judged-by. KEY NUANCE proven empirically: Zod object.safeParse is LENIENT (it STRIPS unknown keys instead of rejecting, and FILLS qualityGate via .default() when absent), so the JSON Schema (additionalProperties:false; qualityGate in `required`) is intentionally STRICTER on inputs than Zod safeParse — exactly matching the old hand-written behaviour and satisfying equivalent-or-stricter. Canonical Zod source of truth: src/schemas.ts workerResultSchema(38), reviewResultSchema(81), overseerDecisionSchema(114).
baseline.toJsonSchemaNotes: zod 4.4.3, z.toJSONSchema is a function and available. Default output emits draft 2020-12 via a top-level `\"$schema\": \"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema\"`; the hand-written schemas had NO $schema, so the generator strips it (`delete json.$schema`) to preserve the exact proven shape. Default io mode is 'output' — this is REQUIRED, not optional: io='input' drops .default()-bearing fields (reviewResultSchema.qualityGate) from `required`, which would loosen the contract; output mode keeps qualityGate required (verified: io:input -> qualityGate in required = false; default -> true). z.toJSONSchema already produces additionalProperties:false on every z.object and correct nested `required` arrays with NO extra options. Only cosmetic differences vs hand-written: (1) $schema key (stripped); (2) key ordering inside each object (generated: type,properties,required,additionalProperties; hand: type,additionalProperties,required,properties) — semantically irrelevant; (3) an extra `\"default\": {...}` annotation on reviewResultSchema.qualityGate (harmless JSON Schema annotation; does NOT loosen since qualityGate stays required; kept verbatim from zod output). Deep-normalized structural comparison (sort keys, sort required arrays, ignore $schema+default) showed ALL THREE roles semantically EQUAL to the hand-written schemas. Output is deterministic/byte-stable across repeated calls (verified).

design.generator:
SO-1 is already fully implemented at HEAD and I verified it end-to-end (tsc clean, tests pass, normalized structural diff = EQUAL for all 3 roles). The generator lives in a small new module X:\repositories\agent-swarm\src\schema-json.ts with three functions:

1. zodToDriverJsonSchema(zodSchema: ZodType): Record<string, unknown>
   - Body: `const json = z.toJSONSchema(zodSchema) as Record<string,unknown>; delete json.$schema; return json;`
   - z.toJSONSchema OPTIONS: none passed (defaults). Default io mode is 'output' and this is LOAD-BEARING, not incidental. In zod 4.4.3 the default already emits additionalProperties:false on every z.object and the correct per-object `required` arrays with NO extra options needed for strictness. The only post-processing is `delete json.$schema` to strip the draft-2020-12 pointer the hand-written schemas omitted.

2. serializeDriverJsonSchema(zodSchema): string
   - Returns `${JSON.stringify(zodToDriverJsonSchema(schema), null, 2)}\n` — 2-space indent + trailing newline, byte-identical format to the prior fs.writeFileSync hand-written strings. Deterministic/byte-stable (verified by running twice).

3. writeSchemaFromZod(schemaPath, zodSchema): void
   - fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(schemaPath), {recursive:true}) + fs.writeFileSync(schemaPath, serializeDriverJsonSchema(zodSchema), 'utf8'). Exact replacement for the inline mkdir+write that each old writer did.

Call-site integration (cli.ts, names/signatures unchanged): import added at cli.ts:26 `import { writeSchemaFromZod } from "./schema-json.js";`. Bodies at cli.ts:6860-6875 now each call writeSchemaFromZod(schemaPath, <role schema>). Unchanged call sites: writeWorkerResultSchema cli.ts:1642 & 2398; writeOverseerDecisionSchema cli.ts:2105; writeReviewResultSchema cli.ts:2651.
design.perRoleNotes:
reviewResult.qualityGate is the one real per-role hazard and it is handled correctly by the default io='output' mode. qualityGate carries a Zod `.default(() => ({...}))` (schemas.ts:95-101). I empirically confirmed: with io='input' z.toJSONSchema DROPS qualityGate from the top-level `required` array (looser than the hand-written contract, which lists it as required); with the default 'output' mode qualityGate STAYS in `required`. Verified generated top-level required for review = ["status","summary","frAcFindings","testAssessment","sourceMutationDetected","stubOrHardcodeRisk","qualityGate","requiredFixes","escalations","recommendation"] — qualityGate present. Side effect of keeping the default: z.toJSONSchema also emits a harmless `"default": {...legacy gate...}` annotation on the qualityGate property. This is a JSON Schema annotation only; it does NOT loosen validation (qualityGate stays in required) and both CLIs accept it. My normalized diff explicitly ignores this `default` key and the stripped `$schema` key; with those ignored, all three generated schemas are STRUCTURALLY EQUAL to the hand-written ones.

Enums: all enums (worker status/frAcCoverage.status; review status/frAcFindings.status/stubOrHardcodeRisk/qualityGate.status/dimensions.dimension+status+risk/escalations.level; overseer status/blockers.level) are emitted as {type:"string", enum:[...]} with the exact member lists matching the hand-written schemas — verified by structural diff.

Lenient-Zod nuance that justifies equivalent-or-stricter: Zod object.safeParse STRIPS unknown keys (so it accepts extra-property inputs) and FILLS qualityGate via its default when absent. The generated JSON Schema (additionalProperties:false everywhere + qualityGate required) is INTENTIONALLY stricter on inputs than Zod safeParse — matching the old hand-written gate. This is correct: the JSON Schema is the held-to contract handed to codex/claude; Zod is the post-hoc judge.

Cosmetic-only differences vs hand-written (all semantically irrelevant): (1) $schema stripped; (2) key ordering inside objects (generated: type,properties,required,additionalProperties vs hand: type,additionalProperties,required,properties); (3) the qualityGate `default` annotation.
design.parityTestPlan:
tests/schema-parity.test.js EXISTS and all 15 tests pass (node --test). ajv is NOT available (not in package.json deps/devDeps — only better-sqlite3, commander, cross-spawn, yaml, zod + type/tsx/typescript dev). So the test uses a self-contained minimal recursive JSON-Schema validator (validateAgainstJsonSchema) covering exactly the constructs the schemas use: object (required + additionalProperties:false + properties), array(items), string(+enum), boolean, number/integer. It imports the GENERATED schema from ../dist/schema-json.js and the Zod oracle from ../dist/schemas.js.

Per role (worker/review/overseer), 5 tests each:
(a) Valid-fixture acceptance: a hand-built valid fixture is asserted Zod-valid (safeParse.success===true) AND accepted by the generated JSON Schema.
(b) Zod-rejects-both: malformed fixtures (missing required field, bad top-level enum, bad nested enum, wrong type for array/boolean, missing nested required) — assert Zod safeParse rejects AND generated schema rejects (equivalent: never accept what Zod rejects).
(c) Stricter-than-lenient-Zod: inputs Zod LENIENTLY accepts (extra unknown top-level key, extra unknown nested key, and for review: missing-defaulted qualityGate) — assert Zod safeParse SUCCEEDS but generated schema REJECTS (proves >= as strict as hand-written).
(d) Structural parity: top-level type==='object', additionalProperties===false, property names deep-equal the Zod shape keys (Object.keys(zodSchema.shape)), required deep-equals the hand-written driver contract (expectedRequired), and a recursive assertNoOpenObjects walks every node asserting every {type:'object'} sets additionalProperties:false.
(e) Determinism: serializeDriverJsonSchema called twice is byte-equal, output does NOT contain "$schema", and ends with a trailing newline.

Beyond the committed test, I independently ran a normalized deep-structural diff (sort keys, sort required arrays, ignore $schema+default) of each hand-written schema (extracted from baseline commit 5328f02:src/cli.ts) against the generated one: worker/review/overseer all normalized-structural-equal === true.

Verification I actually ran (not claimed): npx tsc -> exit 0 clean. node --test tests/schema-parity.test.js -> 15/15 pass. node --test on worker-driver.test.js + review-runner.e2e + claude-reviewer.e2e + claude-worker.e2e + claude-overseer.e2e -> 37/37 pass. tests/overseer-runner.e2e.test.js -> 6 pass / 3 fail, and I confirmed the 3 failures reference codex planning content + overseer prompt size (no schema/additionalProperties/required/safeParse references), matching the documented pre-existing-at-baseline failures; they are unrelated to schema generation.
risks: The qualityGate `default` annotation is emitted into the driver-facing JSON Schema (an extra `"default": {...}` on the qualityGate property). It is a benign JSON Schema annotation and does NOT loosen validation (qualityGate stays in `required`), but it is a real shape difference vs the hand-written schema and both codex (--output-schema) and claude (--json-schema) must tolerate it. The claude-*/codex e2e tests pass, indicating tolerance, but this relies on the CLIs ignoring unknown annotation keys.

Correctness depends entirely on z.toJSONSchema DEFAULTING to io='output'. If a future zod minor flips the default to 'input' (or someone passes {io:'input'}), reviewResult.qualityGate would silently drop out of `required`, loosening the contract below the hand-written baseline. The schema-parity test's review structural-parity assertion (required must include qualityGate) and the 'missing-defaulted qualityGate' stricter-than-Zod test would both catch this regression — good defensive coverage — but the dependency on a library default is implicit.

Key-ordering differs from the hand-written output (generated: type,properties,required,additionalProperties). Semantically irrelevant for JSON Schema validators and the diff confirms equivalence, but any external snapshot/byte-comparison test (none found) would break.

tests/overseer-runner.e2e.test.js has 3 failing tests. I verified they are pre-existing and content/prompt-size related, not schema-related, but a casual `npm test` run will show 3 reds that are easy to mis-attribute to this change.

The parity test relies on a hand-rolled minimal JSON-Schema validator (no ajv). It covers exactly the constructs these three schemas use today; if the Zod schemas later add constructs (oneOf/anyOf, $ref, pattern, format, additionalProperties:true subschemas), the mini-validator could give false-positive parity. Acceptable for current scope but a latent limitation.

impl.summary: SO-1 is fully implemented at HEAD (on top of clean 5328f02) and I re-verified it end-to-end. A new module src/schema-json.ts derives the driver-facing JSON Schema from the canonical Zod schemas via z.toJSONSchema: zodToDriverJsonSchema(zod) -> z.toJSONSchema(zod) with default ('output') io mode, then `delete json.$schema`; serializeDriverJsonSchema -> JSON.stringify(...,null,2)+'\n' (byte-format identical to the prior hand-written strings); writeSchemaFromZod(path, zod) -> mkdir + writeFileSync. The three writers in src/cli.ts (writeWorkerResultSchema:6860, writeReviewResultSchema:6866, writeOverseerDecisionSchema:6872) now delegate to writeSchemaFromZod with workerResultSchema/reviewResultSchema/overseerDecisionSchema — same names, signatures, and all four call sites (cli.ts:1642, 2398, 2105, 2651) unchanged. Import added at cli.ts:26. The Zod schemas in src/schemas.ts were NOT modified. tests/schema-parity.test.js (15 tests, 5/role) asserts equivalent-or-stricter behavior and determinism using a self-contained JSON-Schema mini-validator (ajv is not a project dependency).
impl.generatedVsHandwritten: EQUIVALENT-OR-STRICTER, confirmed by an independent normalized deep-structural diff I ran: I extracted each hand-written schema verbatim from baseline 5328f02:src/cli.ts, normalized both sides (deep-sort object keys; sort `required` and `enum` member arrays; ignore the stripped `$schema` key and the benign qualityGate `default` annotation), and got normalized-structural-equal = true for ALL THREE roles (ALL_EQUAL=true). Findings per role: worker — no `$schema`, no `default` annotation, fully equal. overseer — same, fully equal. review — fully equal apart from the one documented benign difference: z.toJSONSchema emits a `default` annotation on the qualityGate property because reviewResultSchema.qualityGate carries a Zod .default(); I empirically confirmed this does NOT loosen the contract — top-level required still includes 'qualityGate' (verified: required = [status,summary,frAcFindings,testAssessment,sourceMutationDetected,stubOrHardcodeRisk,qualityGate,requiredFixes,escalations,recommendation]; qualityGate.additionalProperties=false; qualityGate.required=[status,summary,dimensions,blockingConcerns,residualRisks]). This output-mode behavior is load-bearing: input mode would drop qualityGate from required (looser). Every nested object sets additionalProperties:false. The only cosmetic deltas vs hand-written are: $schema stripped (matches hand-written, which omitted it — generated output also has no $schema), intra-object key ordering, and the qualityGate `default` annotation. None affect validation. The generated schema never accepts anything the hand-written one rejected.

skeptics.evidence:
VERIFIED from code + actual generated output (zod 4.4.3, z.toJSONSchema built-in).

GENERATOR: src/schema-json.ts:24-28 zodToDriverJsonSchema = z.toJSONSchema(zodSchema) then delete json.$schema. Uses DEFAULT ("output") io mode (documented schema-json.ts:14-19), which keeps additionalProperties:false on z.object and keeps .default() fields required. cli.ts:6860-6864 writeWorkerResultSchema now calls writeSchemaFromZod(schemaPath, workerResultSchema) (the diff replaced the inline hand-written literal).

WORKER ZOD SCHEMA: src/schemas.ts:38-53 — 8 fields, all required (no .optional/.default), nested frAcCoverage item object with ref/status/evidence.

EQUIVALENT-OR-STRICTER (never looser): I ran the generator on workerResultSchema and did a semantic deep-compare (key-order-insensitive, required/enum treated as sets) against BOTH the prior hand-written literal in the cli.ts diff AND the checked-in schemas/worker-result.schema.json (lines 1-51). Result: "SEMANTICALLY IDENTICAL: true". Same 8-key required set; same top enum [passed,failed,blocked,needs_human]; same nested enum [covered,not_covered,blocked]; same nested required [ref,status,evidence]. Only delta vs the checked-in reference file is the stripped $schema/title decorations — strictly cosmetic, not a constraint relaxation (and intentional per schema-json.ts:20-22).
